default_core.summary: Default checks cover only high-frequency AI failure modes with low false-positive rates and high multi-turn compounding risk. Objective checks run deterministically outside the model context window; standing prose stays capped at <= 300 words.
selection_criteria: High observed frequency in coding-agent sessions or public empirical studies.
Low false-positive rate validated against real production OSS commits.
Compounding multi-turn risk if left unchecked (future turns imitate shortcuts or dead paths).
Narrowest prevention layer first: deterministic diff/structural gate -> canonical codebase example -> short standing prompt rule last.

layer_a_diff_checks.summary: Blocks newly added test skip/xfail waivers in test diffs.
Blocks edits under tests/ unless --allow-test-edit is explicitly granted.
Blocks newly added TODO/FIXME placeholder comments in added lines.
Blocks non-abstract NotImplementedError stubs in added lines.
Blocks bare pass placeholders in non-abstract functions.
Blocks blanket lint/type suppression comments without specific rule codes and rationale.
Blocks bare or broad exception catches that silently pass or return empty literals.
Blocks breakpoint(), pdb.set_trace(), and JS debugger leftovers.
Blocks hardcoded local workstation home paths (/Users/<name>, /home/<name>, C:\Users\<name>).
Blocks backticked repo-relative file paths in Markdown that do not exist.
Blocks conversational chatbot praise openers in docs and PR bodies.
Blocks trailing chatbot filler sign-offs in docs and PR bodies.
Flags decorative AI emojis outside fenced code blocks (error with --strict-prose).
Enforces configurable net-LOC diff budget (heuristic default 400; disable with --no-budget).
Enforces configurable touched-file diff budget (heuristic default 10; disable with --no-budget).

layer_b_structural_checks.summary: Flags assertion-free, tautological, or heavily mocked tests lacking real value assertions.
Flags broad catches returning silent literals without logging/re-raising and hardcoded defaults on sensitive env vars.
Flags copy-pasted logic blocks duplicated across production functions or files, including renamed-variable clones.
Flags unreachable constant-False branches, unreferenced *_legacy/*_compat shims, legacy boolean flags, and orphaned helpers.
Flags newly added multi-line commented-out code blocks while allowing short why/invariant comments.
Flags oversized (>60 code lines) or high-branch (>12 branches) functions (heuristic starting thresholds).
Flags diffs growing monolithic files beyond 400 code lines (heuristic starting threshold).
Flags single diffs scattered across more than 3 unrelated production module areas.
Flags static circular module dependency cycles in Python and JS/TS production modules (skipping TYPE_CHECKING, deferred imports, and type-only imports).

Flags speculative single-implementation abstractions (Python ABC/Protocol or JS/TS abstract/interface wrappers with <= 1 concrete implementation, or trivial pass-through *Factory/*Wrapper/*Impl classes).
Flags raw environment-variable reads for the same non-runtime key scattered across 3 or more production modules instead of centralized boundary config validation.

rules.name: Define done
rules.focus: Cover every material requirement; never redefine success to fit output.

rules.name: Ground claims and premises
rules.focus: Verify premises against inspected evidence; distinguish facts from assumptions.

rules.name: Keep scope simple
rules.focus: Reuse sound conventions; avoid speculative abstractions and duplicated logic.

rules.name: Verify and report accurately
rules.focus: Run checks tied to the requirement; never edit or weaken tests to fit broken code.

rules.name: Remove avoidable burden
rules.focus: Cut filler and unnecessary complexity while preserving required caveats.

rules.name: Preserve trustworthy context
rules.focus: Keep canonical sources accurate and correct superseded derivatives.

rules.name: Learn from defects
rules.focus: Fix the defect, keep a reproducible pair, prefer tools over prose, and retire obsolete rules.

optional_packs.name: Network Timeouts
optional_packs.description: Catch outbound HTTP calls written without explicit timeouts in Python and JS/TS code.
optional_packs.when_to_enable: Enable in backend services, CLIs, and workers that make outbound HTTP requests where a hung socket can wedge a worker pool.

rules.title: Python HTTP call without explicit timeout
rules.remediation: Pass an explicit timeout=... argument (for example, timeout=10 or timeout=(3, 10)) so outbound requests fail fast instead of hanging indefinitely.
rules.why_optional: Internal one-off scripts, local fixture servers, or repositories wrapping a custom HTTPAdapter with default timeouts may intentionally omit per-call timeout arguments.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire once Ruff S113 / Bandit B113 or a project-wide HTTP client wrapper enforces timeouts in CI.

rules.title: JS/TS fetch() without AbortSignal timeout
rules.remediation: Pass a signal option (for example, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) } or an AbortController signal) so stalled responses abort cleanly.
rules.valid_neighbouring_case: const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/v1/items", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });
rules.why_optional: Browser UI helpers, local mock handlers, or custom fetch wrappers that inject timeouts centrally may not pass signal: at every call site.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire once an ESLint rule or typed API client wrapper guarantees bounded request timeouts.

optional_packs.name: Security Boundaries
optional_packs.description: Lightweight diff guards for high-confidence Python execution hazards (shell=True, unsafe yaml.load, raw eval/exec). Complementary to full SAST.
optional_packs.when_to_enable: Enable in services handling untrusted inputs or multi-tenant data as a fast local diff guard alongside CI SAST.

rules.title: Python subprocess call with shell=True
rules.remediation: Pass an argv list with shell=False (the default) so untrusted inputs cannot trigger shell injection.
rules.why_optional: Kept opt-in as a focused guard complementary to full SAST; build/ops wrapper repos sometimes invoke shell pipelines intentionally.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire if repo CI already enforces Bandit B602 or Semgrep subprocess-shell rules on every PR.

rules.title: Unsafe yaml.load() without SafeLoader
rules.remediation: Use yaml.safe_load(...) or pass Loader=yaml.SafeLoader to prevent arbitrary object deserialization.
rules.why_optional: Only relevant to Python repos using PyYAML; kept optional so non-YAML projects and dedicated SAST pipelines avoid redundant rules.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire once Ruff S506 / Bandit B506 or PyYAML removal makes this check redundant.

rules.title: Dynamic eval() or exec() in production Python
rules.remediation: Replace eval()/exec() with ast.literal_eval(), json.loads(), or an explicit dispatch table.
rules.why_optional: Code generators, REPL harnesses, and plugin loaders may legitimately use exec(); kept opt-in to preserve low default false positives.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire once Bandit B307/B102 or Ruff S307/S102 enforces this rule in CI.

optional_packs.name: Comment Hygiene
optional_packs.description: Short prompt rule reinforcing removal of dead commented-out code and stale/narrating comments while preserving brief non-obvious invariant explanations.
optional_packs.when_to_enable: Enable alongside deterministic STRUCT-COMMENTED-CODE in repos with legacy commented-out blocks or subtle domain invariants.

rules.title: Delete commented-out code and stale comments; keep brief invariant comments
rules.rule_text: Delete dead commented-out code and line-by-line narrating or stale comments when editing code. Keep only brief 'why' comments that explain non-obvious external invariants, subtle constraints, or edge-case contracts, and verify any comment against the actual code before relying on it.
rules.why_not_deterministic: While STRUCT-COMMENTED-CODE catches multi-line commented-out code blocks deterministically, distinguishing stale or narrating prose comments from genuine non-obvious invariant explanations requires semantic judgment.
rules.remediation: Remove dead commented-out code and redundant narration, fix or delete stale comments that contradict code, and retain short 1-line why/invariant comments.
rules.bad_example:
# Provider delivers strictly in order; remove old timestamp guard
# if event.created_at < sub.last_event_at:
#     return
# Increment counter
count += 1
rules.why_optional: Kept opt-in because blanket comment deletion hurts automated bug-fixing when invariant notes are stripped, and prompt rules remain outside standard/core.md unless proven net-positive on CM1.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire if CM1 multi-model ablation shows zero gain over deterministic STRUCT-COMMENTED-CODE alone, or once models ignore defective commented-out blocks natively.

optional_packs.name: Verification Proof
optional_packs.description: Short prompt rule requiring live end-to-end or real-artifact verification output before claiming completion on apps, APIs, or CLIs.
optional_packs.when_to_enable: Enable in web apps, HTTP APIs, and CLI tools where agents tend to stop after passing heavily mocked unit tests.

rules.title: Require live end-to-end or real-artifact verification before claiming done
rules.rule_text: Before claiming completion on an app, API, or CLI change, execute a real end-to-end command, live HTTP/CLI check, or real-artifact test and report the observed output. Do not rely solely on heavily mocked unit tests as proof of behavior.
rules.why_not_deterministic: Static diff scanners cannot determine whether a given repo has a runnable local server, CLI entrypoint, or sandbox environment capable of live end-to-end execution.
rules.remediation: Run a real CLI/HTTP/artifact smoke check after unit tests and cite the exact command and observed output.
rules.bad_example: Updated the checkout endpoint and all 4 mocked unit tests passed; feature is verified and ready.
rules.valid_neighbouring_case: Ran pytest (12 passed) and posted a real fixture webhook to the local server (HTTP 200, verified balance_due_cents=1106).
rules.why_optional: Pure libraries or air-gapped CI sandboxes may lack runnable live endpoints, whereas app/API/CLI repositories benefit from explicit live-artifact verification.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire once CI integration smoke checks and diff-scoped mutation testing automatically verify changed behavior.

optional_packs.name: Build & Config Hygiene
optional_packs.description: Deterministic guards against floating :latest Dockerfile base tags and world-writable chmod 777 / 0o777 permissions.
optional_packs.when_to_enable: Enable in containerized services and deployment repos where reproducible builds and least-privilege file modes matter.

rules.title: Floating :latest base image tag in Dockerfile
rules.remediation: Pin an explicit version tag or image digest (for example, FROM python:3.12-slim or @sha256:...) for reproducible builds.
rules.why_optional: Disposable local dev containers occasionally track :latest intentionally; kept opt-in so non-Docker or scratch dev setups are unaffected.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire once Hadolint DL3007 or container policy checks enforce pinned base images in CI.

rules.title: World-writable chmod 777 / 0o777 permissions
rules.remediation: Grant least-privilege permissions (such as 755 for executables or 644/600 for data and secrets) instead of world-writable 777.
rules.why_optional: Agents sometimes reach for chmod 777 to bypass container permission errors quickly, but isolated ephemeral build scripts may occasionally have custom mount requirements.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire once infrastructure policy linters (Checkov, Trivy, ShellCheck) enforce least-privilege modes in CI.

optional_packs.name: Architecture Simplicity
optional_packs.description: Short prompt rule discouraging single-implementation factory, interface, and dependency-injection wrapper layers until a second concrete implementation exists.
optional_packs.when_to_enable: Enable in small-to-medium services where over-abstracted multi-file indirection slows down both human readers and bounded-context coding agents.

rules.title: Avoid single-implementation factory/interface/DI wrapper layers
rules.rule_text: Do not introduce abstract interfaces, factory classes, or dependency-injection wrapper layers for a single concrete implementation. Write direct functions or classes first, and extract an abstraction only when a second concrete implementation exists.
rules.why_not_deterministic: Distinguishing a genuine public plugin extension point or test boundary from speculative single-implementation indirection depends on repository architecture and roadmap context.
rules.remediation: Inline single-use factory/interface wrappers into direct functions or concrete classes until a second concrete implementation is required.
rules.valid_neighbouring_case:
def compute_tax_cents(subtotal_cents: int, tax_bps: int) -> int:
    return (subtotal_cents * tax_bps + 5000) // 10000
rules.why_optional: Practitioner hypothesis: plugin SDKs and strict ports-and-adapters enterprise repos intentionally define interfaces upfront; enable only where flat modules fit team norms.
rules.retirement_trigger: Retire if multi-turn benchmarks (EV1) show no maintainability gain or if the codebase adopts an explicit multi-backend plugin architecture.

excluded_considered.title: Statistical AI-text and 'slop' classifiers as CI blockers
excluded_considered.why_excluded: Statistical AI-text detectors misclassify human writing at unacceptable rates, especially non-native English authors (61.22% false-positive rate in Liang et al.), turning CI gates into noisy bias amplifiers.
excluded_considered.what_we_do_instead: Use objective deterministic checks (broken doc paths, chatbot openers/closers, decorative emojis) and warning-first style patterns rather than statistical authorship guessing.

excluded_considered.title: Unfiltered SAST rulesets as blocking post-edit agent hooks
excluded_considered.why_excluded: Firouzi & Ghafari measured default Semgrep and CodeQL rules matching human security ground truth on only 65% and 61% of 1,080 LLM code samples. Running noisy full SAST as a blocking mid-turn hook triggers false-positive churn and workaround loops.
excluded_considered.what_we_do_instead: Keep full SAST in dedicated CI security workflows and offer narrow, high-confidence opt-in diff guards in the security-boundaries pack.

excluded_considered.title: Blanket 'delete all comments' policies
excluded_considered.why_excluded: The ICPC 2026 automated bug-fixing ablation found that indiscriminately removing all code comments degrades bug-fixing effectiveness when helpful intent and invariant notes disappear alongside noise.
excluded_considered.what_we_do_instead: Flag multi-line commented-out code blocks deterministically (STRUCT-COMMENTED-CODE) while preserving short non-obvious 'why / invariant' comments, and measure the tradeoff directly via CM1.

excluded_considered.title: Blanket 'be concise' or 'keep it short' standing prompts
excluded_considered.why_excluded: OpenAI GPT-6.2 guidance warns that legacy 'be concise' instructions strip important uncertainty caveats (uncertainty admission drops sharply), and Anthropic Fable 5.2 docs note rigid style rules produce choppy prose.
excluded_considered.what_we_do_instead: Keep standard/core.md R5 focused on cutting filler while preserving caveats, and isolate model-specific brevity overlays in gates/model_deltas.json only where locally measured.

excluded_considered.title: 100% line-coverage mandates as an AI coding gate
excluded_considered.why_excluded: Coding agents edit tests (23% vs 13% human) and add mocks (36% vs 26% human) more frequently than humans; hard line-coverage targets incentivize assertion-free and heavily mocked test theater that executes lines without catching bugs.
excluded_considered.what_we_do_instead: Detect mock-heavy and assertion-free tests with STRUCT-TEST-THEATER and measure real fault detection via diff-scoped AST mutation testing (anti-slop-mutate and EV1).

excluded_considered.title: Heavyweight upfront dependency-injection and single-implementation abstraction mandates
excluded_considered.why_excluded: Forcing interfaces, abstract bases, and factories for single implementations scatters trivial logic across many files, wasting bounded agent context and encouraging parallel duplicate helpers under context pressure.
excluded_considered.what_we_do_instead: Prefer direct, cohesive implementations by default under R3, and provide OPT-ARC-01 in the optional architecture-simplicity pack for teams that want an explicit prompt reminder.
